articles.body: AI-generated staging can make an empty property look furnished, brightened, or renovated before a prospective buyer ever visits it. From 2 August 2026 , the EU's AI Act transparency regime brings a clear compliance question for businesses using this type of media: when AI generates or substantially alters an image, people must be able to recognise that it is artificial. The rule affects property listings, but it also matters to marketing teams and agencies that publish AI-created visual content in Europe. The legal framework is wider than real estate. Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 defines AI-generated or manipulated content, including deepfakes, in Article 3(60).

articles.body: My Prompt & Theme: Why I Built It for a Friend. This project is built for the Hacktoberfest 2026 Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend. I built Vault specifically for a close relative who works as a lawyer. In the legal sector, professionals handle highly confidential documents, court case files, and private client infrastructure agreements daily. They urgently need AI power to summarize long text files and extract dates, but ethically and legally, they cannot upload these documents to cloud-based AI services like ChatGPT due to strict data privacy laws and third-party data leak risks. Vault explores an alternative: running an open-weight model locally so document contents can be processed directly on the user's own machine.

articles.title: The formula behind every loan EMI calculator, explained plainly
articles.excerpt: Every loan EMI calculator spits out a number, but very few explain where that number comes from. Once you see the formula, you can sanity-check any quote a bank or dealer gives you instead of just tru…
articles.body: Every loan EMI calculator spits out a number, but very few explain where that number comes from. Once you see the formula, you can sanity-check any quote a bank or dealer gives you instead of just trusting the screen. The EMI formula EMI = P x r x (1 + r)^n / ((1 + r)^n - 1) P is the principal you borrow r is the monthly interest rate (annual rate divided by 12, then divided by 100) n is the number of monthly payments That is it. The whole mystery of "equated monthly instalment" collapses into one line. A worked example Say you borrow 500,000 at 8% per year for 20 years. r = 8 / 12 / 100 = 0.006667 n = 20 x 12 = 240 Plug those in and the EMI comes out to roughly 4,182. Over 240 payments you repay about 1,003,680 in total — which means interest alone is around 503,680.
articles.author: abuzar ahun

articles.excerpt: A step-by-step guide to converting narration scripts into broadcast-ready SRT files — zero external dependencies. An SRT file is simple text. Each subtitle block contains four parts: a sequential numb…
articles.body: A step-by-step guide to converting narration scripts into broadcast-ready SRT files — zero external dependencies. The SRT format An SRT file is simple text. Each subtitle block contains four parts: a sequential number, a time range in HH:MM:SS,mmm format, the subtitle text, and a blank line separator. 1 00:00:00,000 --> 00:00:05,200 First subtitle line. 2 00:00:05,200 --> 00:00:10,800 Second line. 3 00:00:10,800 --> 00:00:15,000 Third line, and so on. That is it. No XML, no JSON. Sequential numbers, time ranges, text, blank lines. The blank line between blocks matters — parsers use it as a delimiter.

articles.body: For the Sanity Challenge, I decided to tackle Path One: Ship an agent that queries real content . As someone who builds complex n8n workflows, one of the biggest headaches is API rate limits. When you connect HubSpot, Stripe, and Notion in the same workflow, a simple keyword search like "How to connect HubSpot to Notion" won't save you from a massive 429 Too Many Requests error if you try to sync 5,000 leads at once. Keyword search isn't enough. You need an agent that understands structured constraints and mathematical limits . 🏗️ The Problem If HubSpot allows 100 items per bulk request, but Notion has a strict limit of 3 requests per second, how do you build the workflow? A standard LLM will just give you generic advice.

Judge Amit Mehta noted that the lawsuits weren’t based on a formal agreement with Google, but an “expectation.” This is the second major setback for publishers this year, after a federal court dismissed a similar lawsuit brought against Google. Ed-tech company Chegg filed an antitrust lawsuit against Google last year over AI Overviews and how the feature was affecting website traffic and affiliate revenues. Publisher Penske Media Corporation, known for publications like Billboard , Variety , and Rolling Stone , later filed its own lawsuit against the search giant . A federal judge has now delivered a major setback to both parties.

articles.title: PS3 games hogging storage on your Android device? This ARMSX3 feature is for you.
articles.excerpt: ARMSX3 now plays CHD files, which delivers much smaller file sizes than conventional ISO files.
articles.body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR A recent ARMSX3 update has introduced support for playing games in the CHD format. This compressed format can shave gigabytes off your PS3 game files. The update also offers improved frame generation and fewer stutters in certain PS3 games. PlayStation 3 emulation on Android made major strides in recent months thanks to the ARMSX3 app. However, one potential issue is that PS3 games can hog a ton of space on your Android device. Fortunately, a recent ARMSX3 update helps address this issue. The team behind ARMSX3 recently released v1.0.6 of the emulator on GitHub , and it now supports CHD disc images. CHD (Compressed Hunks of Data) is a compression format that delivers smaller file sizes than conventional ISOs.

articles.body: NASA/Joel Kowsky In this Oct. 1, 2026, photo, a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket and Dragon spacecraft launch from Space Launch Complex 40 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. The spacecraft is carrying NASA astronauts Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Sergey Teteryatnikov to the International Space Station for a long-duration science mission.
